Why we moved our CI from containers back to virtual machines

For five years our continuous integration ran entirely in containers on a shared Kubernetes cluster. Last quarter we moved most of it back to short-lived virtual machines.

The main reason was isolation: several builds needed privileged access to test kernel modules, which forced us to weaken the security settings of the whole cluster.

Build times increased by about 8 percent, but flaky tests dropped by more than half because jobs no longer competed for the same node resources.

We also cut our monthly infrastructure bill by 15 percent, since idle capacity on the cluster no longer had to be reserved for peak load.
